voice.text: Two rocks sat outside all morning. [pause] One in the sun. One in the shade. [pause] Which rock feels warmer? Tap your guess.
<emphasis>The sun warms the Earth.</emphasis> [pause] It warms the land, [pause] the air, [pause] and the water.
Touch the rocks! [pause] The sunny rock is <emphasis>warm</emphasis>. [pause] The shady rock is <emphasis>cool</emphasis> — the tree blocks the sun.
Watch the toy dinosaur. [pause] It <emphasis>blocks</emphasis> the light. [pause] A shadow appears on the other side!
The sun moved. [pause] The shadow moved too — <emphasis>always on the side away from the sun.</emphasis>
Look where the sun is. [pause] Then tap the spot where the shadow will fall. [pause] Sometimes I will ask which spot is cooler, or warmer.
The sun is on the left. [pause] Tap where the shadow will fall.
The sun is on the right. [pause] Tap where the shadow will fall.
One rock is in the sun. One is in the shade. [pause] Tap the cooler spot.
One rock is in the sun. One is in the shade. [pause] Tap the warmer spot.
Yes! [pause] The shadow falls away from the sun.
Yes! [pause] Shade is cooler. The tree blocks the sun.
Yes! [pause] The sun warms that spot.
Not quite. [pause] The shadow is on the other side, away from the sun. The toy blocks the light.
Not quite. [pause] The tree blocks the sun, so the shade is cooler.
Not quite. [pause] The sun shines on the open spot, so that one is warmer.
Lab complete! [pause] Now show what you know.
What makes the toy dinosaur's shadow? [pause] The toy blocks the sun's light, [pause] or, dark stuff leaks out of the toy?
The sun is on the left. Where is the toy's shadow? [pause] On the right, away from the sun, [pause] or on the left, next to the sun?
Which spot feels cooler? [pause] The shade under the tree, [pause] the sunny open spot, [pause] or do they feel the same?
What does the sun warm? [pause] The land, the air, and the water, [pause] or only the land?
The sun moves to the right. What does the shadow do? [pause] It moves to the left, away from the sun, [pause] or it stays next to the sun?
<soft>You know where shadows fall!</soft> [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the sun and the shadow once more.
Lesson done! Now go trace a real shadow outside, in the morning and again in the afternoon.
